d: Big text and strong contrast between text and background, so it can be read across a room.

d: A credit says who made it, where it came from and what you may do with it (its licence). Being online does not make it free to use.

d: A path is the address of a file: the folders you open, from the outside in, then the file.

t: Name a file so you can find it

k: name a file so you can find it a good name says what the file is and has the date as year month day so a list sorted by name is also in date order. start with what it is bean results fractions homework. add the date as year month day such as 2026 10 12. use hyphens not spaces or signs. keep the ending .docx .png . do not type a new one to change the type. words such as final and new stop being true when you save another one. file explorer select the file and press f2 to rename. finder select the file and press return to rename. drive and onedrive right click the file and choose rename.

d: Copy makes a second file. Move takes it to a new place. Delete sends it to a bin, if there is one.

d: A few strong words find more than a whole sentence: the thing, the place and the detail that matters. Then read the results page before you click.

t: Who made it, why and when

d: When pages disagree, compare what you can check about them (author, date, source, purpose), not how they look.

d: A fact can be checked (and can be wrong). An opinion is a view; a good one gives reasons. An advert wants you to buy.
k: fact opinion or advert a fact can be checked and can be wrong . an opinion is a view a good one gives reasons. an advert wants you to buy. ask could i check this ask could people reasonably disagree ask does it want my money or my sign up check facts weigh opinions reasons remember what adverts want. sounding sure does not make something a fact. look for sponsored or paid on pages that look like news. any page sponsored ad paid partnership and buy now are the clues to an advert.

d: Use it when you're not sure what to do or hand in. Many mistakes start with answering a different question.

k: make a plan use it when you understand the task but don t know where to start. a plan can be one line. write your first step only the first. break a big task into three or four parts. stuck on the first step try a smaller or simpler version first. decide how you ll know each part is done. a plan isn t a promise. change it when you learn something. maths try the same question with smaller easier numbers. science list the steps of the method before you start. english jot the three points of your paragraph or essay first. code get one small piece working then add the next.

d: Use it when you've been stuck for a while. First work out what kind of stuck it is.

d: Use it when you finish something or get it back marked. Next time starts here.

d: When it runs but does the wrong thing: be the computer. Step through it by hand and track every value.

d: Before you work it out: round the numbers and guess roughly how big the answer should be, so a wrong answer stands out.

d: During and after: read your answer as a real thing. Does the size, sign and unit make sense?
k: is it reasonable during and after read your answer as a real thing. does the size sign and unit make sense say the answer in words with its unit 400 kilograms . ask is it about the right size check the sign can it be negative here check the unit is it the one the question asked for a neat answer can still be wrong. a messy one can still be right. number a discount can t make a price go up. measurement area is in square units volume in cubic units. probability a probability is between 0 and 1.

d: When you don't know where to start: shrink the problem until you can do it, then grow it back.

d: After: put your answer back into the question and see if it works.

t: Predict, then compare with the data

k: predict then compare with the data before an experiment write what you expect and why. after compare it with what happened. write a prediction with a reason i think because . do the experiment and record what happened. compare did the data match if not ask what that tells you. it s often the most interesting part. don t change the prediction afterwards. a wrong prediction is a result too. practical write the prediction before you touch the equipment. simulation predict before you press run or move the slider. written answer say whether the evidence supports your prediction and how.

d: Before and during: change one thing, measure one thing, and keep everything else the same.
